title: Mycolic acids and FAS-II
dek: C60–C90 α-alkyl-β-hydroxy acids built by FAS-I then FAS-II. InhA is the elongation choke point that INH and ethionamide both occupy — after different activators.
story: Mycobacterial mycolic acids are very-long-chain α-alkyl, β-hydroxy fatty acids (typically C60–C90 in Mtb). FAS-I in the cytosol makes C16–C26 precursors. FAS-II, a dissociated bacterial-type cycle (KasA/B, MabA, InhA, HadAB/BC), elongates the meromycolate chain. Condensation onto the α-chain and subsequent decoration (α, methoxy, keto mycolates; cis/trans cyclopropanes via CmaA/MmaA/PcaA) yield the mature species transferred onto AG or trehalose.

Isoniazid, once KatG-activated, forms an INH–NAD adduct that blocks InhA. Ethionamide, once EthA-activated, does the same endpoint with a different adduct. That shared endpoint is why inhA promoter-up mutants are a two-drug problem.

Trehalose dimycolate (cord factor) and the covalent AG-mycolate monolayer are different uses of the same chemistry. Knocking down mycolate synthesis is cidal in replicating cells because the envelope cannot be finished; resting cells with a completed wall are a different pharmacologic object.
deepTitle: Why the cycle is a genomic object
deep: katG S315T is activation loss — high-level INH-R, InhA intact, ETH often spared. inhA c-15t is more enzyme — low-level INH-R plus ETH cross-R. Treat them as different vectors, not two spellings of INH-R.
Isoxyl and thiacetazone hit mycolate decoration (HadAB, MmaA4) and are historical; they still show up in papers and occasionally in salvage discussions. They are not HRZE.
PcaA cyclopropane synthase mutants alter cord morphology and inflammatory tone. Lipid chemistry is immunology.
Do not bulk-copy Mycobrowser annotations into a DST report. The clinically graded objects are katG, inhA (coding and promoter), and ethA for the ETH branch.

visual.caption: FAS-I feeds FAS-II. INH and ETH converge on InhA after different activators. Mature mycolates go to AG or to TDM.

example.title: Why c-15t is not S315T
example.setup: WGS: inhA c-15t, katG WT. MIC INH 0.25 µg/mL. Team wants high-dose INH plus ethionamide in a longer MDR regimen.

steps.title: Shared endpoint
steps.body: More InhA protein raises the concentration needed for both INH–NAD and ETH adducts.

steps.title: ETH is the wrong rescue
steps.body: Promoter inhA mutants are the canonical ETH cross-R pattern. Do not “add ETH to cover INH.”

steps.title: High-dose INH is a different, gated question
steps.body: Some Hr-TB and older MDR recipes use high-dose INH for low-level alleles. That is guidance-specific, not a licence to ignore the promoter.

example.takeaway: Activation loss versus target overexpression are different INH resistances.

check.prompt: INH and ethionamide share which molecular endpoint?
check.why: Different activators (KatG vs EthA), same enoyl-ACP reductase.

check.prompt: A meromycolate chain of ~C50 condensed with a C26 α-branch is in the C60–C90 mycolate window. Which biosynthetic claim is consistent?

check.why: Two-stage synthesis is the point of the plate.
